subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory filenames and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` when configured, or keep the shipped host-local contract?
rationale: Current docs and tests define host-local session-memory artifacts, while memory-core auto-flush already uses configured user timezone; choosing consistency changes shipped filename/header semantics for some upgrades.

options.title: Use existing userTimezone for session-memory
options.body: Adopt `agents.defaults.userTimezone` for the bundled session-memory date, fallback time slug, and header, with focused tests/docs and no new config surface.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory artifacts
options.body: Preserve the current shipped docs/tests and close or mark this behavior as not planned, accepting the mismatch with configured-timezone auto-flush paths.

options.title: Add a dedicated memory timezone contract
options.body: Introduce a separate memory artifact timezone only if maintainers want memory timestamps to differ from prompt/envelope user timezone despite the extra config surface.

recommendation.title: Use existing userTimezone for session-memory
recommendation.body: Adopt `agents.defaults.userTimezone` for the bundled session-memory date, fallback time slug, and header, with focused tests/docs and no new config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has recent source/history ties to both the configured-timezone memory-core side and the carried current session-memory implementation, making them the best available product-direction router.
